final_recommendation: The room converged on a sealed filing by Friday with Wednesday framework settlement talks, contingent on FINMA clarifying settlement authority given D&O/E&O coverage gaps and directors' uninsured exposure. Public filing was rejected to preserve negotiation leverage and avoid immediate AT1 market contagion.
minority_objections: Bondholder counsel initially pushed for public filing with equity-exhaustion exhibits to maximize market pressure and signal seriousness
Institutional investor resisted any public filing that would signal the entire AT1 market is broken
key_conflicts: Public vs. sealed filing strategy: bondholder counsel wanted public pressure, institutional investor and FINMA wanted sealed to preserve settlement window
Timing of equity-exhaustion argument disclosure: whether to reveal immediately for leverage or hold for negotiation
Settlement authority uncertainty: whether FINMA/Finance Department could negotiate if D&O coverage gaps left directors personally exposed
key_concessions: Bondholder group agreed to sealed filing (abandoning public pressure strategy) in exchange for Wednesday framework talks
FINMA agreed to convene settlement talks with independent counsel and discuss recovery mechanism
Institutional investor accepted delayed filing timeline (Friday) conditional on real settlement movement by end of Q2
red_lines: FINMA: will not concede equity-exhaustion argument on merits; insists contracts explicitly authorize write-down under viability event
Bondholder group: will not announce recovery floor before settlement terms exist
Institutional investor: will not support public filing that signals entire AT1 asset class is broken
All parties: settlement window closes if filing goes public before framework is locked
ignored_or_underweighted_risks: Multi-year discovery costs and litigation duration if settlement fails
Contagion to other European banks' AT1 issuance beyond Deutsche/UBS
Shareholder derivative suits against Credit Suisse directors as parallel litigation track
Reinsurance accumulation across multiple policy years and jurisdictions
Political/regulatory backlash if settlement is perceived as rewarding creditor pressure
downstream_risk_variables: D&O/E&O carrier denial letters and timing of coverage gap realization
Directors' personal capacity to absorb uninsured exposure above policy limits
Market repricing of $300B European bank AT1 capital if settlement fails
FINMA/Finance Department actual settlement authority once insurance gaps are confirmed
Timeline for derivative suits in Delaware and other jurisdictions post-filing
Reinsurance tail duration and severity across three-jurisdiction filing
uncertainty_notes: Critical unresolved: whether FINMA/Finance Department retains settlement authority if D&O carriers deny coverage and directors face uninsured exposure exceeding personal capacity. Also unresolved: actual recovery mechanism framework and whether Q2 timeline is realistic given multi-party coordination. Market repricing dynamics if sealed filing leaks or settlement talks collapse remain unmodeled.

marker_evidence.litigation_likelihood: Three-court filing approved in R1, notice within two weeks, litigation momentum variable climbed from 43→67; entire room structured around filing strategy and settlement as alternative to litigation
marker_evidence.regulatory_legitimacy_challenge: Equity-exhaustion and ultra vires arguments developed across all rounds, but FINMA's legal defense (viability event + contract language) was not fundamentally shaken; challenge was tactical leverage, not consensus on illegitimacy
marker_evidence.creditor_hierarchy_controversy: Hierarchy inversion mentioned multiple times (equity preserved while AT1 wiped, capital stack inverted) but primarily as market-confidence argument, not as the central legal/moral driver of the room's direction
marker_evidence.market_confidence_damage: Repricing of $300B AT1 market, contagion to Deutsche/UBS issuance, and 'burning down the asset class' dominated multiple exchanges; institutional investor's core objection was market-wide damage from public filing
marker_evidence.claims_tail: Multi-year, multi-jurisdiction litigation tail explicitly modeled; insurance observer repeatedly raised reinsurance accumulation, policy-year stacking, and duration as decision factors; claims_tail_severity variable climbed 34→50
marker_evidence.financial_lines_relevance: D&O/E&O coverage gaps, per-occurrence caps, aggregate pools, denial letters, and directors' uninsured exposure were central to settlement authority question and drove R3 convergence; financial_lines_exposure variable climbed 28→45

node: Node 2 - AT1 Creditor Reaction Room (late March 2023, AFTER the UBS rescue and the FINMA-ordered full write-down of Credit Suisse AT1 to zero were announced)
